spec.description: Weather balloons over the Alps, a week of them from six launch sites (8–14 November 2026): each radiosonde's flight drawn at its own heights over the relief, its profile under the map, and its height, temperature and wind on charts that share the moment you point at.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT printf('%.1f °C at %.1f km', coldest, coldest_altitude / 1000) AS coldest
FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/alps-radiosondes/flights.parquet' WHERE serial = '${flight:raw}'

spec.description: The coldest air the sonde measured while rising, and how high.
spec.title: Coldest on the way up

spec.rawSql:
SELECT printf('%.0f km in %d h %02d min', path_km, epoch(last_heard - first_heard)::INT // 3600,
              (epoch(last_heard - first_heard)::INT % 3600) // 60) AS flown
FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/alps-radiosondes/flights.parquet' WHERE serial = '${flight:raw}'

spec.description: How far the balloon went over the ground, from launch to landing (or the last frame heard), and in how long.
spec.title: Flown

spec.rawSql:
SELECT printf('%.1f km at %s', top_altitude / 1000, strftime(top_time, '%H:%M UTC')) AS top
FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/alps-radiosondes/flights.parquet' WHERE serial = '${flight:raw}'

spec.description: How high the balloon went before it burst (or was last heard), and when.
spec.title: Highest

spec.rawSql:
SELECT printf('%.0f m/s (%.0f km/h) at %.1f km', strongest_wind, strongest_wind * 3.6,
              strongest_wind_altitude / 1000) AS wind
FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/alps-radiosondes/flights.parquet' WHERE serial = '${flight:raw}'

spec.description: The fastest the balloon drifted while rising, which is the wind's speed, in m/s and km/h, and how high.
spec.title: Strongest wind on the way up
About the balloons and the data

options.content:
A radiosonde is a small box of sensors and a GPS hung under a weather balloon. Weather services launch them twice a day, at the same hours the world over (about 23:15 and 11:15 UTC for the soundings of 00 and 12 UTC), to measure the air from the ground to the stratosphere for the forecasts. The balloon climbs at about 5 m/s, swelling as the air thins, until it bursts 20 to 37 km up; the sonde falls back under a parachute and is seldom found. All the way it radios a frame a second: where it is, how high, how fast it moves, and the air's temperature.

**On the map**, the flight is drawn at its own heights, half as high again as true, as the relief is, and coloured by height. Under the map, its **profile** charts the heights against the distance flown, with its length, climb, descent and time. Point at the profile and the balloon's place shows on the map and on the charts; point at a chart or the route and the profile follows (the dashboard's shared crosshair). Drag across the profile to measure a stretch, the climb through the jet stream for instance; a double click clears it. The "steepest" grade in its header is the balloon's climb or fall against its drift, not a slope. Tilt and turn the map with the right button or Ctrl+drag.

**Pick a flight** in the table: the link on its launch sets the time range to that flight and the site to its own. The site picker and the time range also pick one, the site's flight that fills most of the range: the other sites launch at the same hours, so switching site keeps the same sounding. Innsbruck launches once a day, at about 03:15 UTC, and its sondes are heard only from about 4 km: the mountains round the Inn valley hide them from the receivers below that.

**Data:** [SondeHub Radiosonde Telemetry](https://registry.opendata.aws/sondehub-telemetry), accessed on 15 November 2026, CC BY-SA 2.0: what amateur receiving stations (radiosonde_auto_rx and other decoders) heard of the sondes the weather services launched from Payerne, München, Innsbruck, Udine, Novara and Cuneo, 8 to 14 November 2026, read once from SondeHub's archive by `datasets/alps-radiosondes/build.sh`. A frame heard by twenty stations is kept once; a flight runs from the launch to the landing, or to the last frame heard (a sonde is often lost behind the mountains a few kilometres up). Heights are the GPS's. SondeHub does not calibrate the sensors' readings: for the official soundings, ask the weather services.

spec.rawSql:
-- Every flight of the week, newest first; the link on the launch sets the time range to the flight and
-- the site to its own, which picks it.
SELECT site_name AS "Site", first_heard AS "Launch", round(top_altitude / 1000, 1) AS "Top (km)",
       path_km AS "Flown (km)", coldest AS "Coldest (°C)", strongest_wind AS "Top wind (m/s)",
       epoch_ms(first_heard - INTERVAL 5 MINUTE) AS from_ms, epoch_ms(last_heard + INTERVAL 5 MINUTE) AS to_ms, site,
       -- Where the map opens on the flight, as the clat and clon variables work it out.
       round((south + north) / 2 - 0.55, 4) AS clat, round((west + east) / 2 + 0.1, 4) AS clon
FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/alps-radiosondes/flights.parquet'
ORDER BY first_heard DESC

spec.description: Every flight from the six sites between 8 and 14 November 2026, newest first: when it was launched (UTC), how high it went, how far it flew, its coldest air and its strongest wind on the way up. Click a launch time to show that flight: the link sets the time range to it and the launch site to its own.
spec.title: The week's flights: pick one

spec.rawSql:
-- Height and rise rate a second, from launch to landing: about 5 m/s up, the burst, then the fall under
-- the parachute, fastest in the thin air high up.
SELECT time, round(altitude / 1000, 3) AS "Height", rise AS "Rise rate"
FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/alps-radiosondes/frames.parquet'
WHERE serial = '${flight:raw}'
ORDER BY time

spec.description: The balloon's GPS height and how fast it rose or fell, a point a second. Rising, a weather balloon climbs at about 5 m/s until the latex bursts in the thin air, 20 to 37 km up; the sonde then falls under its parachute, fast at first.
spec.title: Height (km) and rise rate (m/s)

spec.rawSql:
-- The flight, a row a second from launch to landing: the Route layer joins the rows in time order into one
-- route at its own heights (GPS, metres), and its profile under the map charts them against the distance.
SELECT f.site_name || ', ' || strftime(f.first_heard, '%a %-d %b, %H:%M UTC') AS flight,
       r.latitude AS lat, r.longitude AS lon, r.altitude, r.time,
       r.temperature, r.wind, r.rise
FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/alps-radiosondes/frames.parquet' r JOIN 'http://feeds/datasets/alps-radiosondes/flights.parquet' f USING (serial)
WHERE r.serial = '${flight:raw}'
ORDER BY r.frame

-- The six launch sites.
SELECT site_name AS label, site_latitude AS latitude, site_longitude AS longitude, country
FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/alps-radiosondes/sites.parquet'

spec.description: The balloon's route, a point a second from launch to landing, drawn at its own GPS heights over the Alps (one and a half times as high, as the relief is) and coloured by height. Its profile, under the map, charts the heights against the distance flown, with the length, the climb and the time. Point at the profile, the route or a chart and the others show the same moment; drag across the profile to measure a stretch.
spec.title: The flight at its heights: ${flight:text}

spec.rawSql:
-- The air's temperature a second, as the sonde measured it (SondeHub's readings are not calibrated).
SELECT time, temperature AS "Temperature"
FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/alps-radiosondes/frames.parquet'
WHERE serial = '${flight:raw}'
ORDER BY time

spec.description: The air's temperature as the sonde climbed and fell. It drops about 6.5 °C a kilometre up to the tropopause, some 10 to 12 km up, where it stops falling: above lies the stratosphere. Uncalibrated: SondeHub keeps what the receivers decoded.
spec.title: Temperature (°C)

spec.rawSql:
-- The balloon's speed over the ground: on the way up it drifts with the air, so its speed is the wind's;
-- on the way down the sonde tumbles under its parachute, and its speed is no longer the wind's.
WITH f AS (SELECT * FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/alps-radiosondes/frames.parquet' WHERE serial = '${flight:raw}'),
top AS (SELECT arg_max(time, altitude) AS t FROM f)
SELECT time,
       CASE WHEN time <= (SELECT t FROM top) THEN wind END AS "Rising: the wind",
       CASE WHEN time > (SELECT t FROM top) THEN wind END AS "Falling"
FROM f
ORDER BY time

spec.description: How fast the balloon moved over the ground. Rising, it drifts with the air, so this is the wind at its height: the jet stream at 9 to 12 km, and in November the polar night jet higher up in the stratosphere. Falling, the sonde swings under its parachute and its speed is no longer the wind's.
spec.title: Wind (m/s)
Weather balloons over the Alps: a radiosonde's route at its heights, and its profile

spec.description: Where the balloon was launched. With the time range, it picks the flight: the site's flight that fills most of the range.
spec.label: Launch site
spec.name: site
spec.query: Payerne : 06610, München : 10868, Innsbruck : 11120, Udine : 16045, Novara : 16064, Cuneo : 16113

spec.description: The flight shown: the launch site's flight that fills most of the time range (the links in the table of flights set the range to one). "none" when the site has no flight in the range.
spec.label: Flight
spec.name: flight

spec.__legacyStringValue:
-- The site's flight that fills most of the time range, named by its site and its launch; "none" when
-- the site has none in the range, so that every panel reads no rows.
SELECT __text, __value FROM (
  SELECT site_name || ', ' || strftime(first_heard, '%a %-d %b, %H:%M UTC') AS __text, serial AS __value,
         epoch(least(last_heard, $__timeTo()) - greatest(first_heard, $__timeFrom())) AS overlap
  FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/alps-radiosondes/flights.parquet'
  WHERE site = '${site:raw}' AND first_heard <= $__timeTo() AND last_heard >= $__timeFrom()
  UNION ALL SELECT 'No flight from this site in the time range', 'none', -1
)
ORDER BY overlap DESC
LIMIT 1

spec.description: Where the map looks when the flight changes (the map re-centres on it): the middle of the flight's box, a little south of it, as the camera looks north and the heights rise up the screen.
spec.label: Latitude
spec.name: clat

spec.__legacyStringValue:
-- Where the map looks for the flight (its latitude): the middle of the flight's box, a little south
-- of it, as the camera looks north and the heights rise up the screen.
SELECT v FROM (
  SELECT round((south + north) / 2 - 0.55, 4) AS v, 0 AS o FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/alps-radiosondes/flights.parquet' WHERE serial = '${flight:raw}'
  UNION ALL SELECT 46.3, 1
)
ORDER BY o
LIMIT 1

spec.description: Where the map looks when the flight changes (the map re-centres on it): the middle of the flight's box, a little south of it, as the camera looks north and the heights rise up the screen.
spec.label: Longitude
spec.name: clon

spec.__legacyStringValue:
-- Where the map looks for the flight (its longitude): the middle of the flight's box, a little south
-- of it, as the camera looks north and the heights rise up the screen.
SELECT v FROM (
  SELECT round((west + east) / 2 + 0.1, 4) AS v, 0 AS o FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/alps-radiosondes/flights.parquet' WHERE serial = '${flight:raw}'
  UNION ALL SELECT 9.75, 1
)
ORDER BY o
LIMIT 1
